findings.consequence: The concurrency-safety claim underpinning FR-3/C-5 (that WAL+busy_timeout is load-bearing, not redundant) ships without the corroborating evidence the plan itself specified as part of T5's scope, so a future accidental removal of the hardening has no documented baseline to catch the regression against, and reviewers have to take the mitigation's necessity on faith.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change to PaymentRepository.__init__ weakens or removes the timeout=30.0 / PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL hardening. Because this mitigation is deliberately not exercised by an automated/CI toggle (per the plan's own out-of-scope note) and there is no comment, commit note, or other evidence in this PR that the one-time manual flakiness check (run T5 20-50 times without the hardening and confirm sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked) was ever actually performed, nobody reviewing this PR or a later regression PR can tell whether the hardening was proven necessary or is just defensive boilerplate.
findings.reason: Confirming and interpreting a flakiness demonstration across many iterations requires human judgment rather than a deterministic pass/fail check, and the underlying change is in the concurrency/transaction-semantics area the PR review policy always routes to a developer regardless of confidence.
findings.remediation_direction: Perform the one-time manual hardening-verification step from the plan's Proposed design: temporarily remove PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and timeout=30.0, rerun test_concurrent_duplicate_callbacks_do_not_double_fulfil in a loop (~20-50 iterations) to confirm it becomes flaky with sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked, restore the hardening, and add the one-line comment/commit note recording that confirmation next to the hardening code in repository.py, per plan Task T5.

summary: The diff at HEAD 09bfb86 implements the approved plan's idempotency mechanism faithfully: process_callback() gates fulfilment on record_if_new()'s claim result, releases the claim on fulfilment failure via a new release_for_retry() delete-then-reinsert method, emits a distinguishable duplicate log line, and the new/extended tests exercise FR-1 (completed-duplicate), FR-2 (fail-then-retry, verified indirectly per D6 without adding a new read method), and FR-3/FR-4/C-5 (barrier-synchronized concurrent duplicate across independently constructed PaymentRepository instances). CallbackController and the response contract are untouched, matching AC-2/FR-4 and T3's verification-only scope. No schema change, no lock/coordination primitive, and no new dependency were introduced, consistent with C-1/C-2/C-3. Code-level review found no correctness defects in the claim/release/duplicate logic, the WAL+busy_timeout connection hardening, or the test assertions. One gap was identified: the plan's Task T5 explicitly includes a one-time manual verification (temporarily remove the WAL/busy-timeout hardening, confirm the concurrency test becomes flaky, restore it, and record the confirmation as a comment/commit note next to the hardening code) that has no visible evidence in this diff.
